courses.subject: ORPA
courses.title: Surgical Oral Pathology Seminar
courses.description: This weekly seminar uses unknown cases as the basis for discussion of a variety of biopsy specimens taken from the head and neck. Clinical management of cases also is discussed. Students will develop skills for interacting with their medical and dental colleagues.

courses.subject: ORPA
courses.title: Current Perspectives on Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology
courses.description: This seminar series will focus on current research in oral and maxillofacial pathology (OMP) and related fields. Current scientific literature will be critically reviewed. In addition, students will review historical literature to gain a perspective on the development of OMP as a specialty.

courses.subject: ORPA
courses.title: Advanced Oral Pathology
courses.description: This lecture and clinicopathologic correlation series includes study of the etiology, pathogenesis, clinical, and histopathologic aspects of diseases of the head and neck.

courses.subject: ORPA
courses.title: Surgical Pathology in the Hospital Setting
courses.description: Under the supervision of the hospital pathologists, the student will rotate in anatomic pathology, laboratory medicine, dermatopathology, hematopathology, molecular medicine, surgical specialties, and other elective areas to develop advanced concepts of disease as well as a working relationship with medical colleagues.

courses.subject: ORPA
courses.title: Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology Seminar
courses.description: Course includes developmental disturbances of soft and hard tissues, syndromes, inflammation, immunology, pulp and periapical disease, periodontal disease, tumor-like proliferations, microbial disease, endocrine and metabolic diseases. Also includes odontogenic cysts, salivary gland disease, oral epithelial and mesenchymal neoplasms, bone and joint diseases, nerve muscle diseases, dermatological diseases, and blood diseases.

courses.subject: ORPA
courses.title: Master's (Non-Thesis)
courses.description: Individual research under the direction of a mentor with the intention of publication. Completion of a manuscript and submission is a requirement for an MS degree.
